cur-city-nebelivka.dateNote: Another Trypillia megasite. Its houses appear to have been deliberately burned at intervals and the settlement rebuilt — a pattern that looks nothing like a city failing, and nothing like one succeeding either.

Due to agricultural activity and development, the site has been significantly damaged and no archaeology is visible on publicly available aerial/satellite imagery.

cur-fossil-kiik-koba.dateNote: In 1924 Gleb Bonch-Osmolovsky dug this rock shelter in the Crimean Mountains. He found the burial of an adult Neanderthal and the bones of a small child: among the first Neanderthals found in eastern Europe. They are more than 40,000 years old (over 0.04 million years; Middle Palaeolithic).
cur-fossil-kiik-koba.summary: A rock shelter in Crimea where a Neanderthal was found buried, in 1924.

cur-fossil-mezhyrich.dateNote: In 1965 a farmer making his cellar bigger in Mezhyrich, Ukraine, dug up a mammoth's jawbone. Digs found four huts built from 149 mammoth bones. They are about 0.018–0.015 million years old. Pinned on the village of Mezhyrich.
cur-fossil-mezhyrich.summary: Ice Age huts in Ukraine built from mammoth bones.
